target.what: Number of bottles of Zhenjiang Hengshun (恒顺) vinegar sold/exported to the United States in a full year, all bottle types combined (working interpretation: annual export volume in bottles, latest completed year before cutoff, i.e. 2025; alternative: most recent reported fiscal year or trailing 12 mon

target.cadence: Annual (company annual report; customs statistics monthly/annual)
target.caveats: Ambiguity: 'sold to US' could mean export shipments (FOB) vs. retail sales in US; working interpretation is export shipments from Hengshun to US buyers. Hengshun does not disclose US-specific bottle counts; only total export revenue or tonnage may be available. Bottle size mix (typically 500ml) must

assumptions.falsified_by: Disclosure of regional export revenue showing the US is a much smaller or much larger fraction.

assumptions.applies_when: Converts Hengshun US foreign-trade revenue (CNY) into liters.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Hengshun export prices are at or below the national average, or far above 18 CNY/L.

methods.error: formula: numeric constant 1000 not allowed (only 1 and exponents); make it a named input. If the number only converts units (1000 g per kg, days per year), drop it and set the method's "unit" to the unit the formula then gives (e.g. 'g/day'); code converts it to 'bottle/year'

kept.name: Hengshun share of US-bound Chinese vinegar volume
kept.rationale: Hengshun is China's largest vinegar producer but Chinese vinegar exports to the US are spread across many regional producers and unbranded bulk; the p26-p38 keyword-matched table implies an implausible ~58% share, so we anchor well below it. 12% is consistent with Hengshun being the leading branded
kept.applies_when: Used to convert total China-to-US vinegar volume into Hengshun's US-bound volume.
kept.falsified_by: Retail scan, distributor or customs data showing Hengshun holds a much larger or much smaller share of US Chinese-vinegar volume.

kept.name: Average Hengshun US bottle size
kept.rationale: US distributor catalogues (p79, p81, p87, p89) and the 2022 bill of lading (p43, 550ml) cluster at 500-550ml, with 580ml, 535ml, 300ml and 3L variants; 500ml is the modal retail size for US Asian-grocery Chinkiang vinegar.
kept.applies_when: Converts liters of Hengshun US-bound vinegar into bottle counts.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that US-bound Hengshun shipments are predominantly bulk or large-format (3L+) rather than 500ml retail bottles.

kept.name: US share of Hengshun foreign-trade revenue
kept.rationale: Hengshun's overseas sales span Southeast Asia, Japan, Europe and North America; the US is a major but not dominant market. The p28/p30 table (18.5% US share of a Hengshun-labelled overseas flow) supports a value near 20%, though that table's scope is ambiguous.
kept.applies_when: Used to split Hengshun's 2025 foreign-trade revenue into the US portion.
kept.falsified_by: Disclosure of regional export revenue showing the US is a much smaller or much larger fraction.

kept.name: Hengshun export price per liter (CNY)
kept.rationale: China average vinegar export price is ~1.1-1.2 USD/L (p7, p8, p9); at ~7.1 CNY/USD that is ~8 CNY/L. Hengshun is a premium branded Zhenjiang vinegar, so its export price should sit above the national average, near 10.5 CNY/L. Stated in CNY so it is directly compatible with p48.
kept.applies_when: Converts Hengshun US foreign-trade revenue (CNY) into liters.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Hengshun export prices are at or below the national average, or far above 18 CNY/L.

kept.name: Hengshun export share of total revenue
kept.rationale: Foreign-trade revenue 39.2M CNY (p48) over total revenue 2.29bn CNY (p52) is ~1.7%; this assumption is a cross-check factor for the capacity route, consistent with the observed ratio.
kept.applies_when: Used in the capacity-times-export-share route to scale total vinegar sales to export volume.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that foreign-trade revenue includes substantial non-vinegar products or that export share differs materially.

The volume route multiplies China's total vinegar export volume ([[p1_value]]) by the US share ([[p14_value]]) and by Hengshun's assumed share ([[a1_value]], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]), then converts liters to bottles at [[a2_value]] L per bottle. The company route splits Hengshun's 2025 foreign-trade revenue ([[p48_value]]) by an assumed US share ([[a3_value]]) and export price ([[a4_value]]), then converts to bottles. A third capacity route was dropped for a formula error.

Only the export volume, US share, foreign-trade revenue and vinegar tonnage are observed; the Hengshun share, US revenue share, price and bottle size are analyst assumptions. The interval reflects input uncertainty only, not demonstrated accuracy. The biggest risk is that Hengshun's US-bound volume is largely bulk rather than retail bottles, or that foreign-trade revenue includes non-vinegar goods. US-specific customs or bill-of-lading data for Hengshun would most improve the estimate.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
